q: 61. The natural details are presented on .............
explain: A topographic map depicts natural terrain features (relief, water bodies, vegetation), distinguishing it from a cadastral map which shows land ownership/property boundaries.

q: 62. In case of unidirectional method of dimensioning, they can be read form .............
options: bottom side of drawing sheet only
right side of drawing sheet only
top side of drawing sheet only
left side of drawing sheet only
explain: In the unidirectional dimensioning system, all dimension figures are written horizontally so that they can be read from the bottom of the drawing sheet only, regardless of the direction of the dimension line.

q: 63. Dimension lines and projection line in the drawing are shown by .............
explain: As per drawing conventions, both dimension lines and projection (extension) lines are drawn as continuous thin lines, distinguishing them from thick outlines and dashed hidden lines.

q: 64. System of placing dimension on a drawing work is .............
explain: Dimensions can be placed using either the aligned system (figures aligned with the dimension line) or the unidirectional system (figures always read from the bottom); both are recognized methods.

q: 65. When a drawing is made to the same size of the object, the name of the scale is .............
explain: A scale with representative fraction 1:1, where the drawing size equals the actual object size, is called a full-size (natural) scale.

q: 66. To draw small objects, the scale used is .............
explain: Very small objects (e.g., watch parts) need to be drawn larger than actual size for clarity, requiring an enlarging (enlarged) scale.

q: 67. A letter B in any pencil denotes .............
explain: In the pencil grading system, 'B' stands for blackness/softness of the lead — higher B numbers indicate softer, darker leads, as opposed to 'H' which denotes hardness.

q: 68. Site plans usually show the extent of .............
explain: A site plan's primary purpose is to show the extent (boundaries and layout) of the building site/plot itself, along with the position of structures on it.

q: 69. In perspective drawing, the size of elements depend on .............
explain: In perspective projection, apparent size diminishes with increasing distance from the observer (station point), mimicking how the human eye perceives depth.

q: 70. Maximum ground coverage ratio for hospital building is .............
explain: Building bye-law norms for hospital buildings typically permit a maximum ground coverage ratio of 35%, allowing adequate open space around the structure.

q: 71. The ratio of distance on the drawing sheet and corresponding actual distance of the object is known as .............
explain: The Representative Factor (R.F.) is defined as the ratio of the length of a line on the drawing to the corresponding actual length on the object, expressed in the same units.

q: 72. In isometric projection, the receding lines are drawn with the horizontal at .............
explain: In standard isometric projection, the two receding (isometric) axes are drawn at 30° to the horizontal, with the third axis vertical, giving the characteristic isometric appearance.

q: 73. In orthographic projection, the line of sight and the plane of projection are .............
explain: Orthographic projection is defined by projectors (lines of sight) that are perpendicular to the plane of projection, producing a true, undistorted view of the surface facing that plane.

q: 74. In first angle projection, the object comes .............
explain: First angle projection follows the sequence Observer → Object → Plane, so the object is positioned between the observer and the projection plane.

q: 75. In third angle projection, if the auxiliary vertical plane is placed to the right of the object, the view obtained is called .............
explain: In third-angle projection the plane of projection is placed between the observer and the object; a plane placed to the right of the object captures and directly displays the right side view.

q: 76. A point whose elevation is above XY line may be situated in .............
explain: Since elevation above the XY line only tells us the point is above HP, and this condition can occur along with a top view in front of or behind VP, the point could lie in more than one angle, so 'any of these' fits.

q: 77. A point is 20 mm below HP and 30 mm behind VP. Its top view will be .............
explain: The top view of a point shows its distance behind VP; since the point is below HP, its top view is conventionally drawn above the XY line, at a distance equal to the distance behind VP, i.e., 30 mm above XY.

q: 78. If both the front and the top views of a point lie on the same side of the reference line the point may be situated in following angels .............
explain: When both views fall on the same side of the XY line, the point lies in either the second angle (above HP, behind VP) or the fourth angle (below HP, in front of VP), both of which yield views on the same side of the reference line.

q: 79. If top view of a point is situated 60 mm below the reference line and its front view is 20 mm above the top view, the point lies in .............
explain: A top view below XY indicates the point is in front of VP; a front view further below (only 20mm above the very low top view, i.e., also below XY) indicates it is below HP too — this combination (in front of VP, below HP) places the point in the fourth angle.

q: 80. If a line if parallel to both HP and VP, it true length will be seen in .............
explain: A line parallel to both principal planes is not foreshortened in either projection, so its true length appears in both the front view and the top view simultaneously.

q: 81. If the apparent and the true inclinations of a line with HP are equal, the line is .............
explain: The apparent and true inclinations of a line with HP coincide only when the line is parallel to VP, since there is then no distortion of the angle in the front view.

q: 82. The point at which the line intersects the VP, extended if necessary, is known as .............
explain: The point where a line (extended if necessary) meets the Vertical Plane is called the Vertical Trace (VT) of the line.

q: 83. Set squares are not used to draw .............
explain: Set squares, being rigid triangular tools with fixed straight edges, are used for straight and standard-angle lines but cannot be used to draw irregular curves — that requires a French curve.

q: 84. The diameter of semi-circle is called .............
explain: A protractor's semicircular scale has its straight diametrical edge referred to as the base of the protractor.

q: 85. Drawing pins/cello tapes are used to .............
explain: Drawing pins and cello tape are used to fix (secure) the drawing sheet firmly onto the drawing board so it does not shift while drawing.

q: 86. When only one drawing is to be made then its position should be .............
explain: A single drawing on a sheet is conventionally positioned at the centre of the paper for balanced composition and to leave adequate margins on all sides.

q: 87. Working space on the drawing paper is determined by .............
explain: The border line, drawn inside the sheet's trimmed edges, marks off the usable working (drawing) space on the sheet.

q: 88. The proportion by which the actual size of an object is enlarged or reduced in drawing in simply known as .............
explain: The proportion by which an object's actual size is enlarged or reduced on a drawing is, by definition, called the scale.

q: 89. In case of orthographic projection the number of view generally used are .............
explain: Although a fully described solid could theoretically use up to six principal views, in general engineering practice, orthographic projection typically uses four views (or fewer) — commonly front, top, and one or two side views — to adequately describe an object.

q: 90. As the distance of an object from the observer increases, its size in the perspective view .............
explain: In perspective projection, objects farther from the observer subtend a smaller visual angle, so their apparent size in the perspective view decreases with increasing distance, matching real-world visual perception.

q: 91. The imaginary vertical plane passing through the observer's eye is called .............
explain: The central plane is the imaginary vertical plane passing through the observer's eye (station point) and perpendicular to the picture plane, used as a reference in perspective construction.

q: 92. The imaginary horizontal plane passing through the observer's eye is called .............
explain: The horizon plane is the imaginary horizontal plane that passes through the observer's eye level; its intersection with the picture plane gives the horizon line, on which vanishing points lie.

q: 93. The letter 'H' labeled in a drawing pencil indicates .............
explain: The 'H' grading on pencils denotes relative hardness of the graphite lead — a higher number before H (e.g., 4H) means a harder, lighter lead, useful for fine, thin lines.

q: 94. The technique for freehand sketch to drawing straight line is .............
explain: When sketching a straight line freehand, the recommended technique is to first fix/mark the required length of the line before drawing it lightly between the points.

q: 95. Art of writing title, notes etc. on a drawing is called .............
explain: The skill/art of writing titles, notes, and dimensions on engineering drawings in a standardized, legible style is called lettering.

q: 96. In case of orthographic projection the number of view generally used are .............
explain: As with the earlier repeated question, general orthographic practice commonly uses four principal views (front, top, and side views as needed) to represent an object completely.

q: 97. The main purpose of leader line is in the drawing is .............
options: to connect a note with the feature
explain: Note: per the given answer key, this item's marked answer is 'to show hatch'; however conventionally a leader line is used to connect a note/dimension to the specific feature it refers to on the drawing.

q: 98. The drawing scale of 1 : 25 are best used in .............
explain: A scale of 1:25 provides enough detail for showing reinforcement bar layout in structural/RCC drawings, which require clarity finer than a general building plan scale.

q: 99. If the front view of a line is parallel to the xy line its true length is shown in .............
explain: If the front view of a line is parallel to XY, the line is parallel to the profile plane, and its true length is revealed in the side (profile) view.

q: 100. If a thin set-square is kept perpendicular to both the horizontal and vertical planes, its true shape is seen in .............
explain: A plane perpendicular to both HP and VP is, by definition, parallel to the profile plane (PP), so its true shape appears in the side (profile) view.

q: 101. Size of letter means the ............. of the letter.
explain: In lettering standards, the 'size' of a letter refers to its height, which determines the overall scale/legibility of the lettering on a drawing.

q: 102. The point in space where parallel lines meet is called .............
explain: In perspective drawing, parallel lines receding into the distance appear to converge at a single point on the horizon called the vanishing point.

q: 103. The perspective of a circle. When its plane is parallel to other picture plane, is .............
explain: When a circle's plane is parallel to the picture plane, there is no distortion due to angle, so its perspective projection remains a circle (though possibly scaled).

q: 104. The size of title block of all size drawing sheet is .............
explain: As per drawing standards, the standard title block size used uniformly across all drawing sheet sizes is 185 mm × 65 mm.

q: 105. The artificial light on the drawing board should be diffused light from the .............
explain: For a right-handed drafter, artificial light should come from the left side (diffused) to prevent the drafting hand and instruments from casting shadows over the working area.

q: 106. Circles of small radii are drawn by means of a .............
explain: A bow compass, with its fine adjustment screw, is specifically designed for drawing small circles and arcs with high precision.

q: 107. The following instrument is not used for drawing straight line .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'straight edge' is marked as not used for drawing straight lines in this context; set-squares and the board's working edge are the standard tools/guides actually used for ruling straight lines.

q: 108. Drawing board is made of .............
explain: Drawing boards are made of well-seasoned soft wood, which is light, easy to pin into, and resistant to warping when properly seasoned.

q: 109. During drawing stock of T-square is placed .............
options: adjoining the working edge of the board
adjoining the sliding edge of the board
explain: The stock (head) of the T-square is kept pressed against the working edge of the drawing board, allowing the blade to slide up and down accurately.

q: 110. Planes which are inclined to both the horizontal and vertical planes are called .............
explain: A plane inclined to both HP and VP simultaneously (not perpendicular to either) is termed an oblique plane.

q: 111. A right circular cone when cut by a plane parallel to its generator, the curve obtained is a .............
explain: When a cutting plane is parallel to one generator (slant side) of a right circular cone, the section produced is a parabola, per the standard classification of conic sections.

q: 112. Name the curve traced out by a point on the circumference of a circle, which rolls outside another circle of same diameter .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, this is marked as hypocycloid; conventionally a circle rolling outside another circle of equal diameter traces a cardioid, but the given answer key selects the hypocycloid option.

q: 113. Tracing paper is also named as .............
explain: Tracing paper used in drafting is also generically referred to as drafting media, a term covering various transparent/translucent sheet materials used for tracing drawings.

q: 114. The isometric length of the edge of the cube is obtained by .............
explain: Note: per the answer key this option is marked correct; conventionally the isometric length is obtained by multiplying the true length by the isometric ratio (~0.816), which corresponds to option (c) rather than 'adding.'

q: 115. When a circle rolls inside another circle of twice its diameter, the curve traced out by a point on the circumference of the rolling circle will be .............
explain: A special case of the hypocycloid: when a rolling circle's diameter is exactly half that of the fixed circle, the traced curve degenerates into a straight line (a diameter of the fixed circle) — known as the Tusi couple.

q: 116. Which of the following is not intended while making a sketch in the context of technical drawings?
options: A quick way to record an idea for work
A way to try out different ideas
explain: A technical sketch is meant to be a quick, preliminary tool for recording and exploring ideas — it is explicitly not intended to be a finished, final product.

q: 117. The isometric view of sphere is .............
explain: Since a sphere is symmetric in every direction, its isometric projection (drawn to true/isometric scale) appears simply as a circle.

q: 118. Name the curve traced out by a point on the circumference of a circle, which rolls on another circle of larger diameter .............
explain: Note: per the answer key this is marked 'none of these'; conventionally, a circle rolling on the outside of a larger fixed circle traces an epicycloid, but the given key selects 'none of these' for this item.

q: 119. The angle between isometric axes is .............
explain: Note: per the answer key this item is marked 90°; conventionally, the three isometric axes are mutually inclined at 120° to each other in the standard isometric axis arrangement.

q: 120. First angle projection method and third angle projection method are used in .............
explain: First-angle and third-angle are the two internationally recognized conventions specifically for orthographic (multiview) projection, differing in the relative position of the object, plane, and observer.
